children.text: Cape Engaño Lighthouse is a Spanish-era lighthouse completed in 1892 on a hill about 90 meters above sea level on Palaui Island, the northernmost point of Luzon. You reach it by boat and trek, so the journey itself is an adventure, and from the top the Pacific Ocean and the Babuyan Channel spread out before you.

Cape Engaño Lighthouse stands at the northeastern end of Palaui Island, off Santa Ana, Cagayan. As the northernmost lighthouse on Luzon, it is called a symbol of the northern tip of Luzon, and from its hilltop about

above sea level you look down on the Pacific Ocean and the sea toward the Babuyan Islands. It carries a marker of the National Historical Commission of the Philippines (NHCP) and is classified as an Important Cultural Property. A separate guide covers Palaui Island as a whole, so this guide focuses on how to reach the lighthouse and what to see there. It lies across the sea to the north of the Santa Ana coast, and on clear days the islands of the Babuyan group are said to be visible in the distance.

The lighthouse is one of four built during the Spanish colonial period. Construction began on September 21, 1888 and was completed on December 31, 1892. It was designed by the engineer Magín Pers y Pers, who also designed the Cape Bojeador and Capones Island lighthouses, and most of the laborers are said to have been Filipinos. The name Engaño means deception or illusion in Spanish, and locally it is said that Spanish sailors gave it that name because they were captivated by the beauty of the cape. The tower is an octagonal stone structure, and sources differ on its height, giving anywhere from 11 to 14.5 meters.

The lighthouse consists of a stone tower built with lime mortar and local materials, plus auxiliary buildings. It once carried a copper lantern, and the present light is solar powered, flashing white about every 5 seconds. Its visibility range is given as about 27 nautical miles (about
50km

). The rear living quarters are in ruins, while the storehouse, kitchen and part of the service building remain. One family is said to have lived there for generations as lighthouse keepers. There have also been reports that the Cagayan provincial government is pursuing a restoration project with the economic zone authority, so the site may look different depending on when you visit.

This guide is for travelers planning a visit to the lighthouse, the most iconic stop on a Palaui Island day tour. The journey has three stages: a long trip to Santa Ana, a boat from San Vicente Port and a walk on the island. It depends heavily on the weather and sea conditions, so leave some slack in your schedule and confirm the latest boat fares, guide fees and environmental fee at the local tourism office before deciding. Information about Palaui mixes older and recent reports, so fees and rules differ. The most important thing is to follow the official registration procedure and guide rules for safety and conservation. The lighthouse itself is not a large structure; its appeal is the journey and the location, so go with modest expectations and enjoy the trip itself, and you will come away satisfied.

From the hilltop you are told you can see Babuyan Island and Dos Hermanas, the Two Sisters islands, to the north, the Pacific Ocean to the west, and Engaño Cove to the east. The view opens up best on a clear morning.

An octagonal stone tower completed in 1892. An NHCP marker is attached at the base of the tower, and the site is classified as an Important Cultural Property. Check locally whether you may enter the tower. The whole complex consisted of the tower, living quarters and service buildings such as the kitchen and storehouse, and some of it is now ruins with only the foundations left. Looking at the thickness of the walls and the way the stone is laid, you can imagine how hard the construction must have been.
The route on foot from Punta Verde passes in turn through a coastal village, mangrove forest, an intertidal zone, farmland, forest and grassland. Many reports say the walk usually takes
2–3 hours
. There are stretches with little shade, so be sure to bring water and a hat, and agree on rest points with your guide before setting out.

Some reports say that if the boat lands at Siwangag Cove on the northwest side of Palaui Island, the climb to the lighthouse is relatively short. There are also reports of boats landing close to the lighthouse when the sea is calm, so talk to the boatman first.

Punta Verde, the starting point on the island, has a village and a beach where you can rest before or after the trek. Camping near the lighthouse is said to be restricted, so staying overnight here is the usual choice.
The same boat tour often includes sights such as Anguib Beach, Punta Verde and Pugo Muro. Adding a beach to your day plan helps you recover from the lighthouse trek.

At the northern end of the island there are no buildings to block your view, and the sky opens wide. The scenery is best on a clear morning or around sunset, but moving around after dark is dangerous, so finish your plans while it is still light.

blocks.title: A day tour around one island

children.text: A common format is a boat tour leaving from San Vicente Port that combines the lighthouse, Anguib Beach and Crocodile Island. The tour contents vary by season and by office.

items.title: Day trek to the lighthouse
items.subtitle: From San Vicente Port to the lighthouse

children.text: Take a tricycle from central Santa Ana to San Vicente Port, register at the tourism office and pay the environmental fee.
Cross to Palaui Island by boat in about
45 minutes
. If the sea is rough, departure may be delayed or canceled.
With your guide, walk the trail from the Punta Verde side up to the lighthouse. If you landed at Siwangag Cove, the climb is shorter.
Reach the lighthouse, look around the tower and the ruins, and have lunch while enjoying the view.
Descend by the same path and rest at Anguib Beach or Punta Verde.
Return by boat to San Vicente Port.
It is safest to be back at the port before sunset. Agree on boat and guide times in advance.

items.title: Two-day Palaui itinerary
items.subtitle: Resting at Punta Verde and seeing the lighthouse

children.text: Take a boat from San Vicente Port to the island and leave your bags at your lodging in Punta Verde.
Walk the lighthouse trail with a guide and have lunch near the lighthouse.
Return to Punta Verde, relax on the beach and have dinner at a village restaurant.
In the morning see boat tour stops such as Anguib Beach, then return to the mainland by boat in the afternoon.
Lodgings and restaurants are small, so checking in advance is essential.
The domestic flight from Ninoy Aquino International Airport in Manila to Tuguegarao Airport (TUG) takes about
1 hour
. Routes and schedules change by season.
By bus it is about
10–12 hours
from Manila to Tuguegarao. Some reports mention buses running directly to Santa Ana, but check schedules locally.
Take a van from the Tuguegarao city terminal to Santa Ana. A 2026 guide puts the one-way fare at about
and the journey at
3–4 hours
. Check the date’s fare and last trip at the terminal.
From the Santa Ana terminal to San Vicente Port, take a tricycle for a short ride; one report puts the fare at about ₱15 per person.
Register at the tourism office at San Vicente Port and arrange a boat. The crossing from the port to Palaui Island takes about
45 minutes
Day boat fares vary widely between reports, from ₱1,800 to 3,500 (for a boat of about 8 people). Check the latest fares locally.
The walk from the island to the lighthouse starts at Punta Verde. Going with a guide is recommended.
Departures may be restricted depending on sea conditions and tourism office rules.
March–May, the dry season when the sea is calm, is best for the boat ride and trek on Palaui Island. Midday is very hot then, so plan an early start.

During the rainy and typhoon season (roughly June–November) waves and wind are strong and boats often do not sail. In December–February the northeast monsoon can make the sea rough, so check the weather and tourism office advisories the day before you go.
Visibility from the lighthouse drops greatly when fog or low cloud is present. If the view is your goal, aim for a clear morning.

On the island you can use small guesthouses and homestays in the village of Punta Verde. Facilities are basic and electricity and communications may be limited, so bring what you need. Camping near the lighthouse is said to be restricted, so staying in the village is the usual plan. For bookings, it is more accurate to ask the Santa Ana tourism office or the local lodging directly, and rooms fill up early in peak season.

Food is simple, mostly seafood and rice, served at village restaurants on the island. On a day trip it is safer to bring water, snacks and a packed lunch. There are no shops along the trek. Buy supplies in Tuguegarao or Santa Ana before you set out.
The lighthouse trek usually takes 5–6 hours round trip, so start early in the morning.

per boat for San Vicente to Cape Engaño and a separate
guide for one to four. At the port visitor centre, confirm guide requirements, boat capacity, return time and the total including registration fees.
Bring at least 2 liters of water per person, a hat, sunscreen and comfortable shoes.
Bags may get wet on the boat, so bring a waterproof bag.
Environmental fee payment and registration are done at the tourism office at San Vicente Port. Check the latest rules.
The sunrise and sunset are beautiful here, but avoid moving around at night.
The trip from Tuguegarao to Santa Ana is long, so it is easier to stay overnight in Santa Ana the day before.
Restoration work may be going on, so check just before you visit whether the site is open.
Bring a windbreaker if you plan to rest long at the top of the lighthouse. The wind can be strong on the hilltop.
Mobile signal is weak in places, so save your maps offline.
On days with bad sea conditions, departures are canceled. Leave at least a day of slack and do not make risky crossings.
The trail goes up and down and is very hot at midday. If you are not strong, ask about landing at Siwangag Cove for a shorter climb.
There are almost no hospitals or convenience stores on the island. Bring emergency medicine and snacks.
The inside of the tower and the ruined buildings may be unsafe, so follow the restriction signs.
Fees and rules differ between reports. The figures in this guide come from past reports, so confirm them locally.
When a typhoon approaches, do not stay on the island; return to the mainland early.
The island where the lighthouse stands, with natural attractions such as Anguib Beach and Punta Verde.
A beach often included in Palaui boat tours, good for resting after the lighthouse trek.
